subject.title: Feature Request: Memory Trust Tagging by Source

question: Should OpenClaw define and enforce native memory trust metadata across memory-core/QMD/SDK contracts, or treat trust-tagged memory as an external plugin/MCP responsibility for now?
rationale: The source-level gap is clear, but the security boundary, config shape, default policy, and plugin/core ownership affect durable memory, retrieval authority, and upgrade compatibility, so automation should not choose the permanent design.

options.title: Define native trust contract
options.body: Keep this issue open and have maintainers settle the structured metadata fields, default influence policy, expiration/review behavior, and cross-backend enforcement before implementation.

options.title: Use external MCP/plugin path only
options.body: Document world-model-mcp or a ClawHub memory plugin as the recommended trust-tagged memory path and leave memory-core unchanged for now.

options.title: Split narrower follow-ups
options.body: Keep this issue as the umbrella but route source provenance, autoCapture filtering, retrieval weighting, and UI review surfaces to separate already-linked trackers.

recommendation.title: Define native trust contract
recommendation.body: Keep this issue open and have maintainers settle the structured metadata fields, default influence policy, expiration/review behavior, and cross-backend enforcement before implementation.

likelyOwner.reason: Peter is the strongest available routing signal for the memory SDK/schema/retrieval contract and prior review context on this issue.
